info.title: CivicOS platform API
info.description: Every HTTP endpoint of this installation, generated from its route files (scripts/build-openapi.mjs). Request and response bodies are JSON; errors are `{ "error": string }`. Sign-in rules follow the platform middleware: public sites and public reads are open, everything else needs a session.

post.description: /api/admin/officers/bulk — server-side bulk officer onboarding. Accepts a CSV or JSON array of {email,name,charter_id,role,title?} and forwards to civicos_admin_bulk_create_officers via the service-role client. Returns the substrate's per-row result so the UI can show which entries succeeded and which failed. Auth: callers must hold a platform-tier session OR pass the CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET (so CLI/automation can use it without a UI sign-in). The substrate enforces the platform-tier check separately, so this route is a defense-in-depth gate, not the sole authorisation.

get.description: /api/audit/proof — single-entry verifiable inclusion proof. Given (scope, seq) the endpoint returns: - The audit chain prefix from genesis to seq, so a verifier can re-walk every prev_hash → hash relationship locally. - The targeted entry (== the last row in the prefix). - Every witness attestation that observed (scope, seq), so the verifier can confirm the recorded hash matches what witnesses saw at that time. - A server timestamp framing the proof. The output is the same shape the /api/substrate/export endpoint produces, so it loads directly into /gov/audit-replay (or any third-party copy of lib/audit/replay.ts). Auth: public read. Audit entries are already publicly readable per the RLS policy on civicos.audit_entries.

get.description: The signed-in official's own sign-in activity, newest first (lib/auth/activity.ts): sign-ins with a coarse device, failed attempts against the account, password and second-step changes, administrators' changes to the account.

The signed-in official (register 15.4). GET: who is signed in, how officials sign in on this installation, and whether actions require it. POST signs in — with a platform account (email + password) or, when the substrate is connected, with the substrate's access token, checked by the server and matched to the officer register. DELETE signs out. Every sign-in and sign-out is written to the audit chain; addresses never are.

post.description: Change a platform account (administrators only; audited): disable or re-enable it ({ disabled }), or set its role and institution ({ role, institution }; institution null or "" for the whole government), or reset its second sign-in step when the official's phone is lost ({ resetTwoStep: true }; they set it up again at their next sign-in), or issue a one-time password reset code to hand over in person ({ issueReset: true }; shown once, expires in 24 hours).

get.description: Platform accounts for officials (lib/auth/officials.ts). GET lists them (never password hashes) for a signed-in official. POST creates one: the first account at installation, every later one by an administrator.

post.description: Platform accounts for officials (lib/auth/officials.ts). GET lists them (never password hashes) for a signed-in official. POST creates one: the first account at installation, every later one by an administrator.

Passwords of platform accounts (lib/auth/officials.ts). POST { action: 'change', current, next }: the signed-in official changes their own; every other session of theirs ends and this one is renewed. POST { action: 'reset', email, code, next }: no session; sets a new password with the one-time code an administrator issued (wrong codes count toward the sign-in lockout). The official then signs in as usual. Both audited; passwords and codes never appear in the audit chain.

get.description: The signed-in official's second sign-in step (authenticator app, RFC 6238; lib/auth/officials.ts). GET: whether it is on, whether the installation requires it, and the policy. POST { action }: 'start' → a new key (shown once) and its otpauth:// link; 'confirm' { code } → turns it on, returns ten recovery codes (shown once) and renews the session as having passed the second step; 'off' { code } → turns it off (not when the policy requires it); 'policy' { policy: none | signers | all } → administrators only. Every change is audited. Platform accounts only: substrate officers use the substrate's own sign-in.

get.description: Audit-chain anchoring cron — periodically broadcasts the head of every visible audit scope as a federation event of type 'audit.anchor' on channel 'constitutional'. External systems that subscribe to the federation stream get a continuous live record of where each chain pointed at known wall-clock times. Complements the witness-attestation system: - audit_witnesses table is the append-only, public, tamper-proof record (provable retroactively). - federation 'audit.anchor' events are the realtime broadcast channel (subscribers see it as it happens; consumers can persist externally for an independent record). Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: every 5–15 minutes. Idempotent — anchoring the same head produces an event with the same content, but federation events are append-only so duplicate broadcasts are allowed (consumers dedupe by (scope, seq) if they care).

get.description: Audit-self cron — appends a heartbeat audit entry to the 'substrate:self' scope on each invocation. Pairs with the audit-chain verification: the scope's chain grows continuously, giving the verify_audit_chain coverage sweep a guaranteed sample on every recent run. Also useful as a liveness signal for external monitors observing the audit table.

get.description: Outbound federation webhook delivery worker. For each active civicos.event_webhooks row, finds federation events on its channel newer than its cursor and POSTs each to the registered URL with an HMAC-SHA256 signature header. On an all-2xx run the cursor advances to the last delivered event's at_ms; on the first failure the cursor holds (so the next run retries from the same point) and the failure is recorded. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Delivery is at-least-once per cursor; consumers dedupe on event id. Cadence: recommended every 1–5 minutes.

get.description: Periodic consent auto-expiry. Citizens grant time-bound consents (`expires_at` in the future); past expiry they should flip to 'expired' so officer-side surfaces see them as no-longer-valid and the citizen's wallet doesn't show them as live. civicos.expire_due_consents performs the flip and writes one audit-chain entry per expired consent on the citizen's scope, so the citizen can trace exactly which consent expired and when. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: recommended hourly.

get.description: Per-charter posture aggregator. Reads each activated institution's open pressure (work items + escalations + dispatches), derives a posture / readiness / stress reading, and appends a posture_history snapshot. Designed to run on a slow cadence (every 30 minutes or so); produces a continuous timeline visible on /gov/posture without requiring any operator to manually snapshot.

get.description: Periodic directive-promotion worker — call civicos.promote_due_directives to flip any directive signed for a future effective date to 'effective' once that date arrives. Without this a future-dated directive stays 'signed' forever. Designed for a scheduler (Vercel Cron, Supabase scheduled function, etc.). Protection: shared CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. The secret never reaches the client bundle (server-only route).

get.description: Site feeds cron — every 30 minutes (supabase/cron/schedule.sql). Refreshes the news of every public site whose ministry keeps an existing website with a feed (Link, Embed or Migrate mode). A site whose website is unreachable keeps its last good copy and records the error. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or ?token=), like every /api/cron/* worker.

get.description: Periodic SLA worker — call civicos.escalate_stale_service_requests to surface citizen requests that have been ignored too long. Designed to be hit by a scheduler (cron, Vercel Cron, Supabase scheduled function, etc.) at a regular cadence. Protection: requires a shared secret in the CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET env var, presented either via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. The secret never reaches the client bundle (server-only route).

get.description: Substrate self-metrics emitter. Defines (idempotent) a small set of substrate-level telemetry streams and appends a sample to each on every invocation. Hit periodically by a scheduler — counts become time-series in the substrate's own telemetry tables, visible on /gov/telemetry. Threshold breaches auto-escalate via the existing telemetry → escalation trigger.

get.description: Periodic silent-sensor worker — call civicos.escalate_stale_telemetry_streams to surface active telemetry streams that have stopped reporting. A sensor going silent emits no sample to trip the threshold trigger, so this is the only path by which a blind spot becomes a visible escalation. Designed for a scheduler (Vercel Cron, Supabase scheduled function, etc.). Protection: shared CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. The secret never reaches the client bundle (server-only route).

Manual and uploaded sources are never fetched here. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or ?token=), like every /api/cron/* worker.

get.description: Update watchdog cron — every minute (supabase/cron/schedule.sql). Concludes due probations for every nation: passes a release whose window ended healthy, records overdue health reports as missing, and on a confirmed failure either switches the software back to the last known good release or leaves it waiting for the nation's decision (ask-first, or a release that is not backward compatible). It never installs anything: it can only conclude probations and switch back to the last known good release. The same evaluation also runs when the chamber, a release, the publisher console or the health endpoint is read, as a fallback if the schedule stops. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or ?token=), like every /api/cron/* worker.

get.description: Tamper-detection watchdog. Runs after witness-sweep on the same cadence (or slower) and looks for any audit scope where a recorded attestation disagrees with the live chain. Each divergence becomes: 1. A `civicos.escalations` row at severity 'major', source 'substrate', reason 'witness-divergence:<scope>'. 2. A `civicos.federation_events` entry on channel 'constitutional', type 'audit.divergence', so any subscribed watcher sees it. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: every 15 minutes (same as witness-sweep, but staggered). Idempotent: re-recording the same divergence is silently deduplicated by escalation reason — the operator sees one row, not one per cron tick.

get.description: Witness-sweep cron — emits a substrate-self attestation per visible scope. The substrate becomes its own first witness, so even before any external auditor signs the chain there's a continuous attestation timeline. Any divergence between the cron's recorded hash and the live hash is a tamper indicator. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: recommended every 15 minutes. Idempotent per (scope, seq) — the substrate's unique constraint deduplicates by witness_label.

get.description: One platform directive. POST { action: 'sign' | 'rescind', effectiveAt? } under the named (verified, when signed in) official; audited. A signed-in official signs or withdraws only when they can sign, and only their own institution's directives (lib/auth/roles.ts); drafts are seen only there.

get.description: Directives kept by the platform (lib/data/directives.ts), used when the shared database is not connected. GET lists them (?status, ?issuer, ?limit): drafts only for the issuing institution's officials (all of them while sign-in is neither used nor enforced, as before). POST drafts one under the named (verified, when signed in) official; an official with an institution always drafts for it, and auditors cannot draft.

/api/federation/webhooks/test — send a synthetic signed ping to one registered federation webhook, so an operator can confirm an endpoint is reachable and validates the HMAC signature BEFORE relying on it for real events. The ping is out-of-band: it does NOT advance the delivery cursor and a failure does NOT count toward the circuit breaker. It simply reports the HTTP result back to the caller. Auth: platform-tier officer session OR CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET. The secret lives only in the service-role-readable table, so the signing happens server-side here — the browser never sees it.

get.description: /api/health — diagnostic ping with a substrate reachability probe. Public (no auth) — returns minimal information so it's safe to expose to monitoring systems. Reports: ok flag, substrate-configured flag, substrate-reachable flag (via a cheap count on a public view).

post.description: /api/health — diagnostic ping with a substrate reachability probe. Public (no auth) — returns minimal information so it's safe to expose to monitoring systems. Reports: ok flag, substrate-configured flag, substrate-reachable flag (via a cheap count on a public view).

get.description: The platform's API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document, generated from the route files (npm run build:openapi; a test fails when it falls out of date), so other systems and the nation's own developers can build against it.

A ministry's own case system talking to its queue (lib/data/case-import.ts), authenticated by the system's key (Authorization: Bearer ccf_…), never a session. POST { cases: [{ reference, subject, received, region?, priority?, assignee?, note?, state? }] }: new references are added under the same checks as a loaded file, references this system sent before are updated (state open | assigned | escalated | closed), every refusal comes back by position. GET ?since=<date-time>: what officials did here to this system's cases since then. Every call is audited.

post.description: A ministry's own case system talking to its queue (lib/data/case-import.ts), authenticated by the system's key (Authorization: Bearer ccf_…), never a session. POST { cases: [{ reference, subject, received, region?, priority?, assignee?, note?, state? }] }: new references are added under the same checks as a loaded file, references this system sent before are updated (state open | assigned | escalated | closed), every refusal comes back by position. GET ?since=<date-time>: what officials did here to this system's cases since then. Every call is audited.
Disconnect a case system: POST { action: 'revoke' }. Its key stops working at once; the cases it sent stay. Audited.

get.description: The case systems connected to an institution's queue. GET lists them (never their keys). POST { name } connects one and returns its key once; only an administrator or an official who can sign for the institution may (roles).

post.description: The case systems connected to an institution's queue. GET lists them (never their keys). POST { name } connects one and returns its key once; only an administrator or an official who can sign for the institution may (roles).
Withdraw a load: POST { action: 'withdraw' }. Its cases nobody has acted on leave the queue; cases already assigned, escalated or closed stay. Audited.

get.description: Loading an institution's real cases (lib/data/case-import.ts). GET: the columns a file may have, the earlier loads and how many example cases are still in the queue. POST { csv, fileName?, dryRun?, removeSamples? }: with dryRun, what would be loaded and every refused row with its reason; otherwise the load itself, under the named (verified, when signed in) official, with the file's SHA-256, in the audit chain.

post.description: Loading an institution's real cases (lib/data/case-import.ts). GET: the columns a file may have, the earlier loads and how many example cases are still in the queue. POST { csv, fileName?, dryRun?, removeSamples? }: with dryRun, what would be loaded and every refused row with its reason; otherwise the load itself, under the named (verified, when signed in) official, with the file's SHA-256, in the audit chain.

get.description: An institution's queue. GET reads it (cases age from when they were received; examples are marked source "sample"). POST adds one case typed in by an official (lib/data/case-import.ts: reference, subject, received, region?, priority?, assignee?, note?), checked like a loaded row; audited.

post.description: An institution's queue. GET reads it (cases age from when they were received; examples are marked source "sample"). POST adds one case typed in by an official (lib/data/case-import.ts: reference, subject, received, region?, priority?, assignee?, note?), checked like a loaded row; audited.
Remove the platform's example cases from an institution's queue: POST { action: 'remove' } under the named official; audited. Real cases stay.

get.description: Where the platform keeps its state and when it last saved it (lib/data/persist.ts). Officials only (the access gate requires a session for /api/platform/*).

A public site's content as JSON, for a ministry in Embed mode to place CivicOS services and content on its existing website. Cross-site reads are allowed only for that ministry's registered website; links are absolute.

The editor's view of a public site: its current content (reference record with the nation's published content, placeholders kept), the designs it may use, its versions and proposals, its integration settings, and the languages it can be translated into (the nation's own first).

A public site's published logo (its brand, lib/public-sites/brand.ts), served from the platform. Checked on upload to be a PNG, JPEG or WebP image; served with its own type, no sniffing and no scripts. The address carries a fingerprint of the logo (?v=), so browsers may keep it for a year.

post.description: Ask for email updates from a public site (the newsletter box). Works as a plain form post (answers with a redirect to /subscriptions) or as JSON. Double opt-in: this only queues a confirmation email (lib/data/site-subscriptions.ts).

get.description: A site's text for translation into one language: every translatable string with its English source, the published translation and its status (translated, out of date, missing), and the coverage.

XLIFF 2.0 for a site's translators: download the site's text (with the published translation filled in), and upload the translated file back. An upload is only read and checked here — it becomes a proposal in the editor, which a second official publishes.

post.description: XLIFF 2.0 for a site's translators: download the site's text (with the published translation filled in), and upload the translated file back. An upload is only read and checked here — it becomes a proposal in the editor, which a second official publishes.

get.description: A visitor's language on the public sites: one of the nation's official languages (setup), kept in a cookie for a year, then back to the page they were on. Only a path on this platform is accepted as the way back.

Public institution sites: how each relates to the ministry's existing website (mode, website, feed, redirects) and which design it wears. See lib/data/site-settings.ts and docs/PUBLIC_WEBSITES_PLAN.md.

/api/public/accountability — open-data JSON for the published accountability aggregates (service SLAs, appeals pipeline, decision-time trends, institutional data-access footprint, governance output). Everything here is already anon-readable on the Public Observatory / charter profiles; this exposes it in a machine-readable form so journalists and researchers can consume it programmatically instead of scraping. Aggregate-only (no citizen id, ref, or row-level field). No auth — public by design — and short-cached. Query params: ?days=1..365 (default 90), ?charter=<charter_id> to scope.

/api/public/charters — open-data directory of activated institutions (charters). Pairs with /api/public/accountability: researchers need the charter catalog (id, label, kind, domain) to interpret the per-charter SLA/appeals stats. Institutions are already anon-readable on the Public Observatory; this is their machine-readable form. No auth; short-cached.

/api/public/directives — open-data feed of public directives (signed / effective / rescinded / published). Completes the open-data set alongside accountability, charters, and telemetry. Directives in these statuses are already anon-readable on the Public Observatory; this is their machine-readable form. No auth; short-cached.
/api/public — discovery index for the CivicOS open-data API. Lists the available machine-readable endpoints so a consumer can find them without scraping. Static, long-cached. No auth.

/api/public/telemetry — open-data catalog of active telemetry streams (metadata only: id, charter, label, unit, thresholds). This is what the state measures; sample VALUES are authenticated-tier and deliberately NOT included here. Stream metadata is already anon-readable on the Public Observatory; this is its machine-readable form. No auth; short-cached.

post.description: /api/releases/[id]/decision — a nation's explicit decision on a release: approve, schedule, unschedule, install, skip, reconsider or rollback. Nothing is ever applied without one; each is written to the audit chain.

get.description: /api/releases/[id]/evidence — this nation's compliance evidence pack for a release it can see (manifest JSON with a digest). `download=1` returns it as an attachment. Generating it is audited.

get.description: Substrate digest API — programmatic equivalent of the /gov/substrate "download digest" button. Computes per-view row counts and (optionally) the chain integrity sweep, returning a JSON snapshot. Auth: requires the CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET shared secret (Bearer or ?token=). The endpoint uses the service-role client so counts are global (RLS-unfiltered) — that's what an external archive/auditor wants. Do not expose without the secret.

post.description: Substrate digest API — programmatic equivalent of the /gov/substrate "download digest" button. Computes per-view row counts and (optionally) the chain integrity sweep, returning a JSON snapshot. Auth: requires the CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET shared secret (Bearer or ?token=). The endpoint uses the service-role client so counts are global (RLS-unfiltered) — that's what an external archive/auditor wants. Do not expose without the secret.

get.description: Comprehensive substrate export — compliance / handover artifact. Returns a single self-describing JSON document containing every row the configured service-role client can see across the lifecycle tables. The audit chain is included verbatim so the receiving party can re-verify integrity offline. Witnesses are included so a successor administration inherits the same tamper-after-the-fact proofs. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cost: O(rows). Capped per table via the ?cap query parameter (default 5000, max 50000) so a single response can't blow the lambda budget. Use the existing /api/substrate/digest endpoint for lightweight count snapshots; this endpoint is the full dump.
